description: THE AUTHORISATION FILTER'S TRUE ARM, REACHED CLEAN - the one case in this directory that arrives at app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl:136-143 with the error flag still off and makes that IF fire. Read the filter cases as one set, because no single fixture can carry everything those eight lines do: case06, case08 and case09 drive the filter with a subscript below the valued span, inside the declared table but past the count, and far beyond it, and between them prove the read is bounded; case10 makes BOTH the validation IF and the filter IF fire in one pass and proves the filter is neither gated by the error flag nor an ELSE of the guard above it; this case reaches the filter with nothing having failed first, so the refusal on the screen can only have come from :138-142; and case12 is its controlled comparison, the same stub entry and the same option chosen by an administrator instead, so exactly one byte of input separates a painted refusal from a transfer. The path, statement by statement. The commarea carries CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1, so 88 CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:31 holds, the IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :87 is false, and the MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COMEN1AO at :89 belongs to the branch not taken - this is the REENTER side of gate G38, the ENTER side being case02. :92 receives the map and :93-95 take the DFHENTER arm of EVALUATE EIBAID into PROCESS-ENTER-KEY. The descending test-before scan at :117-121 examines OPTIONI OF COMEN1AI(2:1), finds the '1' of '01' already non-blank and exits at once with WS-IDX = 2, so the two-byte move at :122 into WS-OPTION-X PIC X(02) JUST RIGHT at :45 needs no right-justification and the INSPECT REPLACING ALL ' ' BY '0' at :123 is a no-op. :124 leaves WS-OPTION PIC 9(02) at :46 holding 1 and :125 echoes it into OPTIONO, which is why the echoed field is '01' and not spaces. The three-term guard at :127-129 is then evaluated in source order, gate G30, and every term is false: WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC is false because '01' is numeric; WS-OPTION > CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT is false because 1 does not exceed this case's active count of 1; and WS-OPTION = ZEROS is false because the option is 1. So :130-133 never run, WS-ERR-FLG still holds the 'N' that SET ERR-FLG-OFF TO TRUE at :77 left, and WS-MESSAGE still holds the spaces of :79. Nothing has painted yet, and that untouched precondition is what this case exists to establish. Why the table is a stub, and what the stub varies. app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy:21 declares CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT PIC 9(02) VALUE 10, and every one of the ten valued CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE columns is 'U' (:29, :35, :41, :47, :53, :59, :65, :72, :78, :84). The filter's true arm is therefore UNREACHABLE from the shipped table: no arrangement of real data makes :137 true, and a fixture seeded from the copybook alone could only ever assert that the arm was not taken. The table used here values slot 1 with the copybook's own CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME 'Account View' and CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME 'COACTVWC' literals from :26-28, changes that entry's authorisation column alone to 'A', and declares an active count of 1. The authorisation column is the only variable, which is what keeps the composed OPTN001O line byte-identical to the line the shipped table would produce and stops it becoming a second thing under test. Stated plainly: this case is an assertion about the code, not about the shipped data. The substance. :136-137 carry no IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON guard of their own and are not an ELSE of :127-134, but here that costs nothing, because nothing has failed. The first conjunct, 88 CDEMO-USRTYP-USER at app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:28 VALUE 'U', is true because the commarea supplies CDEMO-USER-TYPE 'U' - load-bearing, because 'A' short-circuits the conjunction before the subscript is ever read and would turn this fixture into case12. The second conjunct reads CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE(1) and finds 'A'. :138 SET ERR-FLG-ON TO TRUE - a SET here where :130 used MOVE 'Y', two spellings of one state that a translation must not let drift apart, and the reason this case asserts the flag rather than assuming it. :139 moves SPACES over WS-MESSAGE, which matters only in proving the literal that follows is not overlaid on anything. :140-141 move the thirty-three-character 'No access - Admin Only option... ' literal, whose trailing space is real and which padding to PIC X(80) makes invisible; the expectation on the WS_MESSAGE_80 channel is that literal followed by exactly forty-seven spaces, eighty characters in total. :142 performs SEND-MENU-SCREEN, and it is the ONLY paint of this pass - which is why the fixture declares one send, and why the message it declares is the refusal rather than the thirty-seven-character 'Please enter a valid option number...' that no branch put there. The suppressed dispatch, and every absence it explains. :145's IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON is false, so the whole of :146-164 is skipped and each of its side effects is missing from the expectation for that one reason: no EXEC CICS XCTL at :152-155, so no successor is named and the termination is the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) of :107-110 rather than a transfer; CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT stays 1 because the MOVE ZEROS at :151 never runs, which is also what makes this response a legal next request; CDEMO-FROM-TRANID and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM keep their inbound 'CC00' and 'COSGN00C' because :147-148 never run; no coming-soon text is composed by the STRING at :159-163; and ERRMSGC is never overridden, because the MOVE DFHGREEN at :158 sits inside that same suppressed block. What makes the suppression airtight rather than incidental is that :138 is the only statement on this path that sets the flag the dispatch is guarded by, so a translation that lost :138 would not merely report the wrong message - it would transfer to COACTVWC and hand the caller the very screen the authorisation column exists to withhold. The colour, which is easy to misread. ERRMSGC is pinned as DFHRED, and that is the map's DECLARED colour rather than something the program moved: app/bms/COMEN01.bms:154-157 is ERRMSG DFHMDF ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET), COLOR=RED, LENGTH=78, POS=(23,1). COMEN01C contains no MOVE DFHRED anywhere in its 282 lines and copies no CSSETATY, so the DFHRED-plus-asterisk field highlight that COACTUPC applies to an offending input has no counterpart here, no xxxA attribute item is written, and no asterisk appears in any expected value. The only colour this program ever moves is DFHGREEN at :158, on the coming-soon path alone, which is how the screen tells a refusal from a confirmation - so a refusal stays red by default, and pinning the attribute rather than omitting it is what keeps that default asserted instead of merely unchecked. The menu lines, and the dead arms that stay dead. BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS at :236-277 loops PERFORM VARYING WS-IDX FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL WS-IDX > CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT, which is this table's 1, so only the WHEN 1 arm at :249-250 fires. OPTN001O is composed by the STRING at :243-246 as CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NUM(1) then '. ' then CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME(1) into WS-MENU-OPT-TXT PIC X(40) at :48, giving '01. ' plus the thirty-five-byte 'Account View' name and one pad byte - forty characters, byte-identical to the first line a full paint would produce. The other eleven lines are the unpainted image, forty U+0000 bytes each and NOT spaces: the MOVE SPACES at :241 targets WS-MENU-OPT-TXT, the WORKING-STORAGE composition buffer, and never a map field, so a line whose arm the loop never reaches simply keeps whatever the map area last held, which is the LOW-VALUES of :89. The WHEN 11, WHEN 12 and WHEN OTHER arms at :269-274 are unreachable here for the same reason they are unreachable with the shipped count of ten, and they are preserved dead code: extending the loop to twelve iterations to 'use' the declared slots would be a behaviour change, not a fix. Geometry a reviewer can confirm by eye, and the defect it exposes. Each table entry is CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NUM PIC 9(02) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME PIC X(35) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME PIC X(08) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE PIC X(01) at app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy:89-92, so 2 + 35 + 8 + 1 = 46 bytes. The data division gives VALUE clauses to ten entries at :25-84, 10 x 46 = 460 bytes, while CDEMO-MENU-OPTIONS REDEFINES CDEMO-MENU-OPTIONS-DATA at :87 spans CDEMO-MENU-OPT OCCURS 12 TIMES at :88, 12 x 46 = 552 bytes - so the redefinition is 92 bytes LARGER than the item it redefines, and slots 11 and 12 have no backing literal at all. Three nested ranges follow, and the filter is unguarded across all of them: what the program calls valid is 1 to 10 (:21), what it declares is 1 to 12 (:88), and what a WS-OPTION PIC 9(02) subscript at app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl:46 can hold is 0 to 99. That oversized REDEFINES is a genuine shipped defect and is preserved rather than repaired, as is the unguarded filter itself: the subscript read is bounded to the declared OCCURS 1..12 so that no Java exception appears where COBOL without SSRANGE would have computed an offset and read stray bytes, and nothing else about either construct is corrected - not resized, not clamped, not guarded, not raised. Because COBOL subscripts are 1-based and Java indices are 0-based, gate G33, subscript 1 must address the FIRST entry, and it is the first entry alone that carries 'A' here - so a translation reading index 1 of a 0-based table would find slot 2's 'U', the filter would not fire, and this case would report a transfer instead of a refusal. Widths, and which channel the message belongs to. Payload names and widths come from the xxxI and xxxO items only: OPTIONI is PIC X(2) at app/cpy-bms/COMEN01.CPY:132, OPTN001O to OPTN012O are PIC X(40) at :182-248 and OPTIONO is PIC X(2) at :254, while OPTIONL COMP PIC S9(4), OPTIONF and OPTIONA at :127-130 and OPTIONC, OPTIONP, OPTIONH and OPTIONV at :250-253 are length, flag and attribute metadata and are never payload members. The message is pinned at the eighty bytes of WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) at app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl:38 and deliberately NOT at the seventy-eight of ERRMSGO PIC X(78) at COMEN01.CPY:260: the truncating MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :187 loses the last two bytes and is case16's subject, and manufacturing a seventy-eight-byte field here would assert this fixture's own arithmetic instead of the program's. Every value is written out to its full declared width in US-ASCII rather than trimmed, because a trimmed expectation cannot tell a padded field from a short one. Statelessness, security and determinism. Every scrap of conversation state arrives in the request - EIBCALEN 160, the DFHENTER AID byte reproduced by common.CicsAid because DFHAID is IBM-supplied and absent from this repository, risk R-D, the sixteen-field CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and the received OPTIONI - and leaves in the response's navigation image; nothing is held server-side, which is gate G37. The unit kind is SERVICE, so admin.MainMenuService is constructed and called as a plain object with no MockMvc, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path, which is gate G51. CDEMO-USER-TYPE is trusted exactly as the source trusts it: :149-150, MOVE WS-USER-ID TO CDEMO-USER-ID and MOVE SEC-USR-TYPE TO CDEMO-USER-TYPE, are commented out and are the program's only mention of any SEC-USER-DATA field, so no USRSEC read re-verifies the type, nothing is hashed, and the single PIC X(01) comparison at :137 is the entire authorisation mechanism. That posture is left visible rather than quietly improved, and the bounded read is emphatically not treated as a security control. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:33, the instant every case in this directory pins and the one app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl's own version footer carries, and the code page is named US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default. Honestly about that clock: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :212-231 does run, because SEND-MENU-SCREEN performs it at :184, and it composes CURDATEO as WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY and CURTIMEO as WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS from app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy:30-41 - but the SERVICE projection carries only the twelve menu lines and the echoed option, so neither field is surfaced here. The pinned instant buys determinism, not an assertion; the header fields belong to the CONTROLLER_POJO cases case01, case16 and case20. Provenance, and what this case does not prove. Every value above is STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl, app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, app/cpy-bms/COMEN01.CPY, app/bms/COMEN01.bms and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:399-400, which defines TRANSACTION(CM00) PROGRAM(COMEN01C). None of it was captured from a live COBOL execution: no z/OS or CICS runtime exists in this environment, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, refuses a PROCEDURE DIVISION USING under -x, fails to parse app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy and offers no Language Environment CEE services - eight verified blockers in all, recorded as risk R-A. A statically derived expectation can encode a misreading where a captured one cannot, so the limits are stated rather than glossed. What this case decisively proves: the filter's true arm is reachable with the error flag off; :138 is a SET and it is the statement that sets the flag; the refusal image is the thirty-three-character literal padded to eighty; the dispatch at 146-155 is suppressed, so no successor is named; ERRMSGC keeps the map's red because :158 never runs; exactly one send happens; and the run reports RETURN-CODE 0, which is the only value any of this program's three terminations can produce, since COMEN01C has no CALL 'CEE3ABD', no ABEND and no RETURN-CODE of its own. What it does NOT prove, on its own: that nobody hoisted the filter into the validation's ELSE or gave it the IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON test it lacks, because a guarded filter would produce this exact output when nothing failed first - that regression is caught by case10 and by the MainMenuService unit tests rather than here; that the subscript read is bounded, which is case06, case08 and case09; that the seventy-eight-byte ERRMSGO narrowing is right, which is case16; and that the coming-soon composition is right, which lives on the paths this error flag suppresses. One divergence is recorded rather than silently resolved: an alternative design for this slot would have driven OPTION 13, one past the declared OCCURS 12, as a further boundary anchor; this slot is committed to the true arm reached clean, the two subjects cannot share one fixture because a rejected option cannot also be a clean reach, and the 13 anchor is held instead by the twelve-slot model assertions together with case08 at 11 and case09 at 99. Gates pinned: G15, G18, G30, G33, G37, G38 on its REENTER side, and G51. HOW THE OPTION TABLE IS ARRANGED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA: app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy carries 'U' in all ten of its CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE columns, so the true arm of the authorisation filter at app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl:136-137 cannot be reached from the shipped table at all, and the OCCURS 12 slots past the populated range are storage rather than data that no dataset seeds. The table is therefore the one input to this program that cannot be expressed as a seeded row, which is why unitStimulus.environment.MENU_TABLE_VARIANT declares it. Each variant differs from the shipped table in exactly ONE column, so the authorisation column is the only variable under test and every composed menu line stays byte-identical to the real one. It is declared here rather than chosen by an adapter that recognised this file's case identifier, because an adapter keyed on an ordinal means this file gives no indication which table it runs over and renumbering it would silently move the arm to a different case. An unrecognised variant is refused by the adapter rather than ignored. This case declares ADMIN_ONLY_FIRST_ENTRY: the copybook's first entry with its authorisation column changed to 'A' and nothing else, offered as the only active option. Option 1 is within the active count, so the guard at 127-134 does not fire and the filter is reached clean; CDEMO-USER-TYPE 'U' makes the first conjunct true and the run is refused. Which arm the adapter asserts is decided by the option standing WITHIN the active count and by 88 CDEMO-USRTYP-USER holding, not by this file's name.
